title: Actual Poisson rejection output and auxiliary-query cost
source_anchor: arXiv:2609.06906v1 Appendix A.1 Lemma A.2; arXiv:2608.05022v1 Algorithm 1 and Theorem 2.3
target_statement: For a measurable parameter space S, a Markov proposal kernel Q:S to X, auxiliary probability Xi on A, jointly measurable W:S times X times A to Real bounded in [-B,B] for a fixed B>0, and a default output x0, construct the actual independent one-attempt law from Q(s), Poisson(2B), an iid Xi stream and Uniform[0,1]. Read exactly the first N auxiliary coordinates and accept with the product of (B+W)/(2B). Prove the conditional acceptance probability exp(w(s,x)-B), w(s,x)=integral W(s,x,z) Xi(dz), and the accepted submeasure Q(s).withDensity(ofReal(exp(w(s,.)-B))). Its mass p(s) is positive and at least exp(-2B). On an actual iid sequence of whole attempts, construct the total first-success output with default x0 on never-success; prove that never-success has zero mass, the preceding-failure tail is (1-p(s))^m, and the output law is Q(s).tilted(w(s,.)), forming a measurable Markov kernel in s. Prove the actual full-batch accumulated auxiliary-query count including the successful attempt has expected value 2B/p(s)<=2B*exp(2B). Do not assume independence of the current acceptance event and its Poisson count.
